thread:
Maya Chen: Quick ask — can we temporarily enable full response-body capture for a single prod session to debug a regression where the model is emitting what looks like API keys and other secrets?
Alex Romero: short answer: we need sec sign-off + a scoped retention window. also preferred: never store raw tokens that match key-like patterns.
Maya Chen: understood. thinking: capture one-hour window, store encrypted, and run an automated scrub that redacts token-looking strings before any human sees them. Is that sufficient or do we need an exception ticket? @sec-team
sec-bot: Security policy reminder: any logs containing secrets require an explicit approval and must be stored in a restricted bucket with access audit. Hashing/hmac is preferred over plaintext.
Riley Singh: ops here — we can spin up ephemeral capture for 60m, put results in a dedicated S3 prefix with SSE-KMS, and set lifecycle to delete after 24h. We can also restrict IAM to an allowlist.
Maya Chen: thanks. Proposed scrub plan (pre-human): 1) remove any header values named Authorization, Cookie. 2) regex redact on body for patterns: `(?:sk|pk|ak|vk|secret)[-_]?[A-Za-z0-9]{24,}` and email-like strings replaced with `<REDACTED_EMAIL>`. 3) hash remaining long alphanumeric tokens with HMAC-SHA256.
Alex Romero: that regex is a decent start. Please also consider false positives — e.g., commit hashes. For hashes we can prefix with `<HASH>` after HMAC. Also don't log full prompts if they contain user PII.
Maya Chen: good point. We'll exclude full prompt text for any requests flagged with `user_pii=true` metadata. For the rest, capture response snippet up to first 200 chars after scrub.
Riley Singh: ops checklist: we need (a) sec approval message in thread, (b) ticket in internal tracker with retention and purpose, (c) KMS key id for bucket, (d) list of individuals who need access. I can prepare infra once we have approval.
Alex Romero: sec: +1 on that checklist. Also request that any captured artifacts are uploaded only via an approved uploader that runs the scrub pipeline before upload.
sec-bot: auto-note: Please follow the temporary capture SOP (doc link: https://intranet/redwood/sec/temp-capture). Failure to scrub is a policy violation.
Maya Chen: Ok I'll: create ticket, add KMS key, add preliminary allowlist (myself, Alex, Riley), and post the approval here. Aim to run capture tomorrow 09:00 UTC for one hour.
Riley Singh: I'll prep the bucket and the upload hook. ops-bot will run a dry run in staging.
ops-bot: deploy-check: staging dry run succeeded, scrub pipeline removed 3/3 simulated tokens.
Alex Romero: from sec: I approve contingent on the scrub being applied prior to any human access. Post the ticket link here and we can proceed. :thumbsup:
Maya Chen: will do — creating ticket now and will paste link. thanks everyone.
